claim: MAVS protein forms prion-like aggregates mediated by the N-terminal caspase activation and recruitment domain (CARD).
source: Mitochondrial antiviral signaling (MAVS) protein forms prion-like aggregates mediated by the N-terminal caspase activation and recruitment domain (CARD) and activates antiviral signaling cascades.
evidence: This is stated as established background information in the introduction without specific experimental data in this manuscript.

claim: MAVS activates antiviral signaling cascades.
source: Mitochondrial antiviral signaling (MAVS) protein forms prion-like aggregates mediated by the N-terminal caspase activation and recruitment domain (CARD) and activates antiviral signaling cascades.
evidence: This is stated as established background information in the introduction.

claim: Purified MAVS CARD from culture cells self-assembles into filaments.
source: Purified MAVS CARD from culture cells self-assembles into filaments.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge from prior work.

claim: A low-resolution cryoEM structure of MAVS CARD filament was previously reported with C3 symmetry with a rotation of −53.6° and an axial rise of 16.8 Å for every unit in the filament.
source: Previously, we reported a low-resolution cryoEM structure of MAVS CARD filament, which exhibits a C3 symmetry with a rotation of −53.6° and an axial rise of 16.8 Å for every unit in the filament (Xu et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim references a prior publication by the authors (Xu et al., 2014).

claim: A cryoEM reconstruction of MAVS CARD filaments at 3.6 Å resolution was reported with a C1 helical symmetry of a rotation of −101.1° and an axial rise of 5.1 Å per subunit.
source: Recently, a cryoEM reconstruction of MAVS CARD filaments at 3.6 Å resolution was reported with a C1 helical symmetry of a rotation of −101.1° and an axial rise of 5.1 Å per subunit (Wu et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim references a publication by Wu et al., 2014.

claim: The helical ambiguity in helical reconstruction was not fully resolved in the previous analysis by Xu et al., 2014.
source: The differences in these two models were carefully analyzed recently (Egelman, 2014), which suggested that the helical ambiguity in helical reconstruction was not fully resolved in our previous analysis (Xu et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim references an analysis by Egelman, 2014.

claim: A 4.2 Å resolution reconstruction of MAVS CARD filaments purified from mammalian cells under native conditions was obtained using a newly developed method for analysis of helical filaments.
source: Using a newly developed method for analysis of helical filaments (Clemens et al., 2015), we obtained a 4.2 Å resolution reconstruction of MAVS CARD filaments purified from mammalian cells under native conditions.
evidence: This claim is supported by the experimental data presented in the manuscript and references the method from Clemens et al., 2015.

claim: The new model shows that the MAVS CARD filament exhibits a C1 helical symmetry in agreement with Wu et al. (2014).
source: The new model shows that the MAVS CARD filament exhibits a C1 helical symmetry in agreement with Wu et al. (2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by the experimental reconstruction data and references Wu et al., 2014.

claim: CryoEM images of Flag-tagged MAVS CARD (residues 1–100) protein were collected using automated data acquisition in a Titan Krios with a Falcon II direct electron detector.
source: CryoEM images of Flag-tagged MAVS CARD (residues 1–100) protein, which was expressed in HEK293T cells and purified as described previously (Xu et al., 2014), were collected using automated data acquisition in a Titan Krios with a Falcon II direct electron detector (Figure 1A; see 'Materials and methods' section for detail).
evidence: This describes the experimental method used in the study.

claim: Fourier transforms of motion-corrected raw images showed Thon rings up to ∼3 Å.
source: Fourier transforms of motion-corrected raw images showed Thon rings up to ∼3 Å (Figure 1B–C).
evidence: This claim is supported by the data shown in Figure 1B-C.

claim: 15,600 out of 27,915 boxed filament segments were used to calculate the final refined map.
source: 15,600 out of 27,915 boxed filament segments were used to calculate the final refined map.
evidence: This describes the data processing for the final map calculation.

claim: The new dataset converged better to the C1 symmetry.
source: We found that the new dataset converged better to the C1 symmetry.
evidence: This is based on the computational analysis of the experimental data.

claim: The refinement converged to helical parameters of ΔΦ = −101.21° and Δz = 5.06 Å.
source: After the fifth run, the refinement was continued to optimize the helical parameters and converged to (ΔΦ = −101.21° and Δz = 5.06 Å) (Figure 2A), close to the C1 symmetry reported by Wu et al. (2014).
evidence: This is supported by the refinement data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The final map has an overall resolution of 4.18 Å, estimated from the gold-standard Fourier Shell Correlation (FSC) calculated between two maps that were refined independently against the top and bottom halves of the dataset.
source: The final map has an overall resolution of 4.18 Å, estimated from the gold-standard Fourier Shell Correlation (FSC) calculated between two maps that were refined independently against the top and bottom halves of the dataset (Figure 2B; see 'Materials and methods' section).
evidence: This is supported by the FSC analysis shown in Figure 2B.

claim: A B-factor weighted map based on the PDB model from Wu et al. (2014) (PDB ID: 3J6J) yielded an estimated resolution of 4.25 Å at 0.5 FSC threshold.
source: To examine the resolution with an independent method, we generated a B-factor weighted map based on the PDB model from Wu et al. (2014) (PDB ID: 3J6J), and used it to calculate FSC against the experimental map. A 0.5 threshold found an estimated resolution of 4.25 Å (Figure 2C), close to the one estimated by using two halves of experimental data (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by the FSC analysis shown in Figure 2C and comparison with Figure 2B.

claim: The new map showed clear grooves in α-helices and multiple bulky side chains.
source: The new map showed clear grooves in α-helices and multiple bulky side chains (Figure 2D, Video 1).
evidence: This is supported by the structural features visible in Figure 2D and Video 1.

claim: The six α-helices of the crystal structure of MAVS CARD monomer (PDB: 2VGQ, residues 3–93) fitted into the EM map well.
source: While the six α-helices of the crystal structure of MAVS CARD monomer (PDB: 2VGQ, residues 3–93) fitted into the EM map well, multiple bulky side chains and those residues in the loop between H4 and H5 needed adjustment.
evidence: This is based on the fitting of the crystal structure into the cryoEM map.

claim: Multiple bulky side chains and those residues in the loop between H4 and H5 needed adjustment when fitting the crystal structure into the EM map.
source: While the six α-helices of the crystal structure of MAVS CARD monomer (PDB: 2VGQ, residues 3–93) fitted into the EM map well, multiple bulky side chains and those residues in the loop between H4 and H5 needed adjustment.
evidence: This is based on the fitting analysis of the crystal structure into the cryoEM map.

claim: The atomic model reported previously (PDB: 3J6J, residues 1–97, Wu et al., 2014) fit into the density well except for some unoccupied densities next to the N- and C-termini of the docked CARD model.
source: The atomic model reported previously (PDB: 3J6J, residues 1–97, Wu et al., 2014) fit into the density well except for some unoccupied densities next to the N- and C-termini of the docked CARD model (Figure 2A,D).
evidence: This is based on the fitting of the Wu et al. model into the new cryoEM map, as shown in Figures 2A and 2D.

claim: The extra densities next to the N- and C-termini may be due to the residues from the N-terminal Flag tag and the additional three residues at the C-terminus of the protein used for preparing the cryoEM specimens.
source: These extra densities may be due to the residues from the N-terminal Flag tag and the additional three residues at the C-terminus of the protein used for preparing the cryoEM specimens; these extra residues are not present in the protein sequence shown in the atomic models.
evidence: This is an inference based on the known composition of the protein construct used.

claim: Each MAVS CARD monomer interacts with six nearby monomers using three types of intermolecular interfaces (I, II and III).
source: From the high resolution C1 map, each MAVS CARD monomer interacts with six nearby monomers using three types of intermolecular interfaces (I, II and III) (Figure 3A; Wu et al., 2014).
evidence: This is based on the structural analysis of the high-resolution C1 map shown in Figure 3A and referenced to Wu et al., 2014.

claim: Interface I is mainly mediated by electrostatic interactions.
source: At interface I, the positive and negative charges are distributed at two opposite ends of each CARD subunit, indicating that this interface is mainly mediated by electrostatic interactions (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is inferred from the charge distribution observed in the structure shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The positively charged residues R37 and R41 in H3, R64 and R65 in the loop between H4 and H5 from one CARD molecule are in close proximity to the negatively charged residues D23 in the loop between H1b and H2 and E26 in H2 of another CARD molecule at interface I.
source: The positively charged residues R37 and R41 in H3, R64 and R65 in the loop between H4 and H5 from one CARD molecule (grey in Figure 3B) are in close proximity to the negatively charged residues D23 in the loop between H1b and H2 and E26 in H2 of another CARD molecule (cyan in Figure 3B).
evidence: This is based on the structural analysis shown in Figure 3B.

claim: D23A mutation showed significantly decreased activity compared with wild-type MAVS.
source: Compared with the wild-type MAVS, which potently induced IFNβ in a dose-dependent manner, D23A showed significantly decreased activity and mutations of other charged residues (E26, R37, R41, R64 and R65) at the interface to alanine or residues with reversed charge almost completely abolished MAVS activity (Xu et al., 2014).
evidence: This is based on functional data from the previous study (Xu et al., 2014).

claim: Mutations of charged residues E26, R37, R41, R64 and R65 at interface I to alanine or residues with reversed charge almost completely abolished MAVS activity.
source: Compared with the wild-type MAVS, which potently induced IFNβ in a dose-dependent manner, D23A showed significantly decreased activity and mutations of other charged residues (E26, R37, R41, R64 and R65) at the interface to alanine or residues with reversed charge almost completely abolished MAVS activity (Xu et al., 2014).
evidence: This is based on functional data from the previous study (Xu et al., 2014).

claim: In the crystal structure of MAVS CARD, the aromatic chain of W56 adopts two alternative conformations, with a major conformer (60% occupancy) exposed to solvent and stacked against the ring structure of residue F16 in immediate vicinity.
source: In the crystal structure of MAVS CARD, the aromatic chain of W56 adopts two alternative conformations, with a major conformer (60% occupancy) exposed to solvent and stacked against the ring structure of residue F16 in immediate vicinity (Potter et al., 2008).
evidence: This is based on the crystal structure from Potter et al., 2008.

claim: In the cryoEM map, the density of one conformer of W56 is resolved.
source: In the cryoEM map, the density of one conformer is resolved (Figures 2D, 3D) and there appears density corresponding to the side chain of R43 from an adjacent CARD (Figure 3D), suggesting a possible cation–pi interaction between these two residues, as reported previously (Wu et al., 2014).
evidence: This is based on the cryoEM density shown in Figures 2D and 3D.

claim: There appears density corresponding to the side chain of R43 from an adjacent CARD in the cryoEM map, suggesting a possible cation–pi interaction between R43 and W56.
source: In the cryoEM map, the density of one conformer is resolved (Figures 2D, 3D) and there appears density corresponding to the side chain of R43 from an adjacent CARD (Figure 3D), suggesting a possible cation–pi interaction between these two residues, as reported previously (Wu et al., 2014).
evidence: This is based on the cryoEM density shown in Figure 3D and inference about the interaction, with reference to Wu et al., 2014.

claim: Alanine substitution of R43 almost completely abolished MAVS activity.
source: Alanine substitution of R43 almost completely abolished MAVS activity (Xu et al., 2014).
evidence: This is based on functional data from the previous study (Xu et al., 2014).

claim: Single alanine substitution of F16, W56 or Y30 almost completely abolished MAVS activity.
source: Single alanine substitution of F16, W56 or Y30 almost completely abolished MAVS activity, while substitutions with different ring-containing residues to these positions, such as F16H, W56F, W56Y, Y30F and Y30H, were able to largely retain MAVS activity (Xu et al., 2014).
evidence: This is based on functional data from the previous study (Xu et al., 2014).

claim: Substitutions with different ring-containing residues to positions F16, W56, and Y30, such as F16H, W56F, W56Y, Y30F and Y30H, were able to largely retain MAVS activity.
source: Single alanine substitution of F16, W56 or Y30 almost completely abolished MAVS activity, while substitutions with different ring-containing residues to these positions, such as F16H, W56F, W56Y, Y30F and Y30H, were able to largely retain MAVS activity (Xu et al., 2014).
evidence: This is based on functional data from the previous study (Xu et al., 2014).

claim: R52 is involved in stabilizing interface II.
source: Another residue involved in stabilizing the interface is R52, whose replacement by alanine significantly decreased its activity (Xu et al., 2014).
evidence: This is inferred from the functional data showing that R52A mutation decreased activity.

claim: Replacement of R52 by alanine significantly decreased MAVS activity.
source: Another residue involved in stabilizing the interface is R52, whose replacement by alanine significantly decreased its activity (Xu et al., 2014).
evidence: This is based on functional data from the previous study (Xu et al., 2014).

claim: Interface III mediates the interactions between adjacent monomers along the helical trajectory.
source: Interface III mediates the interactions between adjacent monomers along the helical trajectory.
evidence: This is based on the structural analysis of the filament.

claim: Residue L48 from each MAVS CARD monomer contributes to the formation of a hydrophobic core with G50 and A44 in close proximity at interface III.
source: Close to the central pore of the helical filament, residue L48 from each MAVS CARD monomer contributes to the formation of a hydrophobic core with G50 and A44 in close proximity (Figure 3A, top view and Figure 3E).
evidence: This is based on the structural analysis shown in Figures 3A and 3E.

claim: Substitution of L48 with charged residues (D or K), but not alanine, completely abolished MAVS activity in HEK293T cells.
source: Substitution of L48 with charged residues (D or K), but not alanine, completely abolished MAVS activity in HEK293T cells (Xu et al., 2014).
evidence: This is based on functional data from the previous study (Xu et al., 2014).

claim: L48 is not conserved, and is R or Q in MAVS from multiple other species.
source: It is interesting to note that L48 is not conserved, and is R or Q in MAVS from multiple other species.
evidence: This is based on sequence comparison across species.

claim: The filaments might need to rearrange in order to accommodate substitutions at L48.
source: The filaments might need to rearrange in order to accommodate such substitutions.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the structural constraints and sequence variation.

claim: The small side chain or hydrophobicity of A44 may be important for the packing at the hydrophobic interface because its mutation to T impaired MAVS CARD filament formation in vitro.
source: The small side chain or hydrophobicity of A44 may be important for the packing at this hydrophobic interface because its mutation to T impaired MAVS CARD filament formation in vitro (Xu et al., 2014).
evidence: This is an inference based on functional data from Xu et al., 2014.

claim: Charged residues R37, R41, D40 and D53 are located at the outer rim of the filament forming electrostatic interactions together with charged residues at type I interface.
source: Charged residues R37, R41, D40 and D53 are located at the outer rim of the filament forming electrostatic interactions together with charged residues at type I interface.
evidence: This is based on the structural analysis of the filament.

claim: Single alanine substitution of R37, R41, D40 and D53 almost completely abolished MAVS activity.
source: Single alanine substitution of these residues almost completely abolished MAVS activity (Xu et al., 2014).
evidence: This is based on functional data from the previous study (Xu et al., 2014).

claim: The loss-of-function mutation data are consistent with both the C1 map reported here and the C3 map obtained previously.
source: Overall, the loss-of-function mutation data are consistent with both the C1 map reported here and the C3 map obtained previously (Xu et al., 2014).
evidence: This is an inference based on comparison of the mutation data with both structural models.

claim: Although key residues involved in the interactions are almost identical in the two models, the detailed interactions at the interfaces are different according to the two maps.
source: However, although key residues involved in the interactions are almost identical in the two models, the detailed interactions at the interfaces are different according to the two maps, indicating that mutagenesis analyses alone cannot distinguish one model from the other.
evidence: This is an inference based on comparison of the C1 and C3 models.

claim: Mutagenesis analyses alone cannot distinguish the C1 model from the C3 model.
source: However, although key residues involved in the interactions are almost identical in the two models, the detailed interactions at the interfaces are different according to the two maps, indicating that mutagenesis analyses alone cannot distinguish one model from the other.
evidence: This is an inference based on the comparison of the two models and the mutation data.

claim: MAVS CARD filaments from the new dataset converged to almost the same C1 symmetry as reported by Wu et al. (2014), not the C3 symmetry as reported previously by Xu et al. (2014).
source: MAVS CARD filaments from our new dataset converged to almost the same C1 symmetry as reported by Wu et al. (2014), not the C3 symmetry as we reported previously (Xu et al., 2014).
evidence: This is based on the new experimental data and analysis presented in this manuscript.

claim: The heterogeneity of the samples and the limited resolution of images were likely among the factors that led to the exclusion of the C1 model in the original analysis.
source: The heterogeneity of the samples and the limited resolution of images were likely among the factors that led to the exclusion of the C1 model in the original analysis.
evidence: This is speculation about the reasons for the error in the original analysis.

claim: The in vitro mapping of the oligomerization interface, cell-based mutational analyses, super-resolution SIM imaging of MAVS aggregates in virus-infected cells, and the crystal structures from the original paper remain valid.
source: We stand by all other data in the paper, including in vitro mapping of the oligomerization interface, cell-based mutational analyses, super-resolution SIM imaging of MAVS aggregates in virus-infected cells, and the crystal structures.
evidence: This is a statement affirming the validity of other data from the original paper.

claim: The experiments in the original paper for the first time identified most of the key residues involved in MAVS polymerization.
source: These experiments for the first time identified most of the key residues involved in MAVS polymerization, leading to an extensive mapping of the molecular surfaces for forming the MAVS filament.
evidence: This is a statement about the contribution of the original paper.

claim: The experiments in the original paper led to an extensive mapping of the molecular surfaces for forming the MAVS filament.
source: These experiments for the first time identified most of the key residues involved in MAVS polymerization, leading to an extensive mapping of the molecular surfaces for forming the MAVS filament.
evidence: This is a statement about the contribution of the original paper.

claim: Flag-MAVS CARD (1–100) was expressed in HEK293T cells.
source: Flag-MAVS CARD (1–100) expressed in HEK293T cells was purified in a buffer containing 50 mM NaCl.
evidence: This describes the experimental method used.

claim: Flag-MAVS CARD (1–100) was purified in a buffer containing 50 mM NaCl.
source: Flag-MAVS CARD (1–100) expressed in HEK293T cells was purified in a buffer containing 50 mM NaCl.
evidence: This describes the experimental method used.

claim: Freshly purified protein was processed for EM experiments to minimize bending and overlapping of filaments on cryoEM grids.
source: Freshly purified protein was processed for EM experiments to minimize bending and overlapping of filaments on cryoEM grids.
evidence: This describes the experimental approach used.

claim: Movie data were collected in a FEI Titan Krios microscope equipped with a Falcon II detector at the HHMI Janelia Farm Research Campus.
source: Movie data were collected in a FEI Titan Krios microscope equipped with a Falcon II detector at the HHMI Janelia Farm Research Campus.
evidence: This describes the experimental method used.

claim: The microscope was equipped with a Cs corrector (Cs = 0.01 mm) and operated at 300 kV.
source: The microscope was equipped with a Cs corrector (Cs = 0.01 mm) and operated at 300 kV.
evidence: This describes the experimental method used.

claim: Images were taken using a defocus range of −2.5 to −4.0 microns at a nominal magnification of 59,000×.
source: Images were taken using a defocus range of −2.5 to −4.0 microns at a nominal magnification of 59,000×, which corresponds to a calibrated pixel size of 1.05 Å at the specimen level.
evidence: This describes the experimental method used.

claim: The nominal magnification of 59,000× corresponds to a calibrated pixel size of 1.05 Å at the specimen level.
source: Images were taken using a defocus range of −2.5 to −4.0 microns at a nominal magnification of 59,000×, which corresponds to a calibrated pixel size of 1.05 Å at the specimen level.
evidence: This describes the experimental method used.

claim: Images were taken with a total dose of 35 e−/Å2 distributed over 16 frames.
source: Images were taken with a total dose of 35 e−/Å2 distributed over 16 frames.
evidence: This describes the experimental method used.

claim: Frames 3–12 of every movie were summed together as the corrected image.
source: Frames 3–12 of every movie were summed together as the corrected image (Figure 1A).
evidence: This describes the data processing method used.

claim: The motion between consecutive frames was very small (mostly less than 2 pixels) due to the carbon-support of the filaments.
source: The carbon-support of our filaments made the motion between consecutive frames very small (mostly less than 2 pixels) and we therefore did not do motion correction for individual filaments (polishing) in Relion.
evidence: This is an observation from the data processing.

claim: Motion correction for individual filaments (polishing) in Relion was not performed.
source: The carbon-support of our filaments made the motion between consecutive frames very small (mostly less than 2 pixels) and we therefore did not do motion correction for individual filaments (polishing) in Relion.
evidence: This describes the data processing approach used.

claim: The analysis started with 27,916 filaments.
source: We started with 27,916 filaments.
evidence: This describes the data processing.

claim: After 2D classification, 15,600 filaments were selected.
source: After 2D classification, 15,600 filaments were selected.
evidence: This describes the data processing.

claim: During the 3D classification into two different classes, there was a negligible fraction of the filaments conforming to a different volume with poor alignment statistics.
source: During the 3D classification into two different classes, there was a negligible fraction of the filaments conforming to a different volume with poor alignment statistics.
evidence: This describes the data processing results.

claim: All 15,600 filaments were kept for final map calculation, which correspond to ∼80,000 images of individual CARD units.
source: We therefore kept all 15,600 filaments for final map calculation, which correspond to ∼80,000 images of individual CARD units.
evidence: This describes the data processing.

claim: The 15,600 filaments were divided into the top and bottom two halves to calculate a gold-standard FSC from truly independent datasets.
source: In order to calculate a gold-standard FSC from truly independent datasets, we divided the 15,600 filaments into the top and bottom two halves.
evidence: This describes the data processing method used.

claim: The two half datasets had negligible overlap.
source: These two datasets had negligible overlap.
evidence: This describes the data processing approach.

claim: Two separate C1 models were generated using the SPIDER-based method from a small sorted fraction (∼13%) of filaments out of the old datasets.
source: Two separate C1 models were generated using the SPIDER-based method from a small sorted fraction (∼13%) of filaments out of our old datasets as described before (Xu et al., 2014), and imposed with diagonally varied symmetry parameters (5.22 Å, −102.2°) and (4.82 Å, −100.2°), respectively.
evidence: This describes the data processing method used.

claim: The two refinements converged to almost the same symmetry parameters, (5.05 Å, −101.25°) and (5.08 Å, −101.20°), respectively.
source: The two refinements converged to almost the same symmetry parameters, (5.05 Å, −101.25°) and (5.08 Å, −101.20°), respectively.
evidence: This describes the results of the data processing.

claim: Wild-type MAVS potently induced IFNβ in a dose-dependent manner.
source: Compared with the wild-type MAVS, which potently induced IFNβ in a dose-dependent manner, D23A showed significantly decreased activity and mutations of other charged residues (E26, R37, R41, R64 and R65) at the interface to alanine or residues with reversed charge almost completely abolished MAVS activity (Xu et al., 2014).
evidence: This is based on functional data from the previous study (Xu et al., 2014).
